name: Loan monthly payment
description: Computes the fixed monthly repayment on an amortizing loan using principal×(mrate/100)/(1−(1+mrate/100)^(−months)). It spreads principal and interest evenly over the term.
notes: Rate is the monthly (not annual) percentage; divide an annual rate by 12. Months is the total number of payments. Assumes a fully amortizing fixed-rate loan.

name: Loan Balance After k Payments
description: Computes the outstanding loan balance after k payments as the compounded original principal minus the future value of the payments already made. It shows how much of the loan remains at a point in time.
notes: The rate r must be per payment period and entered as a decimal; k is the number of payments completed. Assumes a fixed payment and constant rate throughout.

name: Total Interest Paid on Loan
description: Computes the total interest paid over the life of a loan as the sum of all payments (payment times number of payments) minus the original principal. It shows the total cost of borrowing beyond the amount borrowed.
notes: Assumes a fully amortizing loan with a fixed payment for all n periods. It gives total interest only, excluding fees or charges; it is not a per-period figure.

name: Loan-to-Value Ratio
description: Computes the loan-to-value (LTV) ratio as the loan amount divided by the appraised property value, times 100. Lenders use this percentage to gauge risk when underwriting a mortgage.
notes: Loan amount and property value must be in the same currency. A lower LTV generally means less lender risk and can qualify a borrower for better rates.

name: Mortgage affordability
description: Gives a rough borrowing limit by multiplying annual income by an income multiple, a common rule of thumb for how large a mortgage might be affordable.
notes: This is only a screening heuristic; actual approval depends on interest rates, existing debts, deposit, and lender criteria. The multiple varies by market.

name: Loan Amortization Payment
description: Computes the fixed periodic payment on a fully amortizing loan of principal P at rate r per period over n payments, using P*r/(1-(1+r)^(-n)). Each equal payment covers interest plus principal so the balance reaches zero after n periods.
notes: The rate r is per payment period, not annual, so divide an annual rate by the payments per year. All three inputs must use the same period; a monthly loan needs a monthly r and n counted in months.

name: Remaining Loan Balance
description: Gives the outstanding loan balance after k payments as the compounded original principal P*(1+r)^k minus the future value of the payments already made, PMT*(((1+r)^k-1)/r). The result is the principal still owed.
notes: The rate r is per period and k is the number of payments already made, both on the same schedule. PMT must be the actual periodic payment; a mismatched payment leaves a rounding residual in the balance.

name: Number of Payments to Pay Off a Loan
description: Solves the annuity formula for the number of level payments needed to repay a loan.
notes: The payment must exceed the interest r·PV, otherwise the loan is never repaid. Here about 41.0 payments.

name: Rate of an Annuity (Solve for r)
description: Finds the periodic interest rate implied by a loan amount, payment and term — what spreadsheet RATE() computes — by solving the annuity equation numerically.
notes: Multiply by 12 for a nominal annual rate on monthly payments. Here about 0.0088 per period.

name: Mortgage Monthly Payment (Annual Rate, Years)
description: Gives the level monthly payment of a fully amortising loan from its annual nominal rate and term in years.
notes: 300,000 at 6 % for 30 years costs about 1,798.65 a month.

name: Total Interest over a Mortgage
description: Adds up all interest paid over the life of a level-payment loan.
notes: The 300,000 loan at 6 % over 30 years costs about 347,515 in interest.

name: Interest Part of Payment k (Amortisation)
description: Splits payment number k of a level-payment loan and gives its interest part (spreadsheet IPMT).
notes: Early payments are mostly interest: the first of 1,798.65 contains 1,500 of interest.

name: Principal Part of Payment k (Amortisation)
description: Gives the part of payment k that repays principal (spreadsheet PPMT); it grows by the factor (1 + r) each period.
notes: In month 120 of a 30-year 6 % loan about 546 of the payment goes to principal.

name: Cumulative Interest Paid in Payments 1 … k
description: Adds the interest paid in the first k payments (spreadsheet CUMIPMT): total paid minus principal repaid.
notes: In the first five years of the 30-year 6 % loan about 87,574 goes to interest.

name: Equal Principal Repayment: Payment k
description: Gives payment k when the same amount of principal is repaid every period (declining payments) plus interest on the outstanding balance.
notes: The first payment is 833.33 + 1,500 = 2,333.33; payments fall steadily to about 837.5.

name: Equal Principal Repayment: Total Interest
description: Gives the total interest with equal principal repayments: interest on a balance falling linearly from P to P/n.
notes: Less than a level-payment loan (270,750 against about 347,515 here), because principal is repaid faster.

name: Affordable Loan from Income (DTI Limit)
description: Gives the largest loan whose monthly payment stays within a share of gross monthly income (the front-end debt-to-income limit).
notes: The widely used 28 % rule with 90,000 income, 6 % and 30 years allows about 350,000.

name: Debt-to-Income Ratio
description: Divides all monthly debt payments by gross monthly income.
notes: Lenders commonly look for 36 % or less (43 % for many qualified mortgages).

name: Mortgage Points Break-even
description: Gives the months needed for the lower payment bought with discount points to repay their cost.
notes: Buying points pays off only if you keep the loan longer than this (here about 48 months).

name: Interest-Only Payment
description: Gives the monthly payment of an interest-only loan, which repays no principal.
notes: 300,000 at 6 %: 1,500 a month, and the full 300,000 is still owed at the end.

name: Add-on Interest Loan Payment
description: Gives the monthly payment of an add-on loan, where interest on the full amount for the whole term is added up front and divided equally.
notes: The true APR is almost twice the add-on rate, because the balance falls while interest was charged on the original amount.

name: True APR of an Add-on Loan
description: Finds the annual percentage rate actually paid on an add-on loan by solving for the monthly rate that its payments imply.
notes: A 6 % add-on over 4 years is about 11.0 % APR.

name: Credit Card Payoff Time
description: Gives the months needed to clear a credit-card balance with a fixed monthly payment and no new charges.
notes: 5,000 at 22 % APR paid at 150 a month takes about 50 months.

name: Credit Card Payment to Clear in n Months
description: Gives the fixed monthly payment that clears a credit-card balance in n months.
notes: To clear 5,000 at 22 % in two years takes about 259 a month.

name: Minimum-Payment Trap: Balance after k Months
description: Tracks a card balance when only a fixed percentage of the balance (after interest) is paid each month.
notes: At 2 % minimum and 22 % APR, 5,000 only falls to about 3,240 after five years.

name: Average Daily Balance Finance Charge
description: Computes the finance charge for a billing cycle from the average daily balance.
notes: 2,400 average balance at 20 % for 30 days costs about 39.45.

name: Payday Loan APR
description: Converts a flat fee on a short loan into an annual percentage rate.
notes: A 15 fee per 100 for two weeks is about 391 % APR.

name: Rule of 78 Interest Rebate
description: Gives the unearned interest refunded when a precomputed loan is repaid early, by the Rule of 78 (sum-of-digits).
notes: Front-loads interest: after half the term only 21/78 of the charge is refunded here (323.08). Banned for many long consumer loans.

name: Loan-to-Cost Ratio
description: Divides a construction or development loan by the total project cost.
notes: Construction lenders often cap it at 75–85 %.

name: Combined Loan-to-Value (CLTV)
description: Adds all loans secured on a property and divides by its value.
notes: Here 90 %. Many lenders require 80 % or less to avoid mortgage insurance.

name: Home Equity
description: Gives the owner's equity in a property: market value minus the loans secured on it.
notes: Lenders typically let owners borrow against equity up to a combined 80–85 % of value.

name: Loan Balance after k Payments (Annual Rate, Monthly)
description: Gives the balance still owed after k monthly payments on a level-payment loan specified by annual rate and term.
notes: After 10 years of a 30-year 6 % loan about 250,886 of 300,000 is still owed.

name: Biweekly Payments: Years to Pay Off
description: Paying half the monthly payment every two weeks makes 26 half-payments (13 monthly payments) a year; this gives the resulting payoff time.
notes: A 30-year 6 % loan is paid off in about 24.1 years.

name: Extra Payment: Months Saved
description: Gives how many months sooner a loan is repaid if a fixed extra amount is added to every monthly payment.
notes: Adding 200 a month to the 30-year 6 % loan saves about 70 months.

name: Car Lease Monthly Payment
description: Gives a lease payment as the depreciation charge plus the finance charge (money factor times the sum of cost and residual).
notes: Taxes and fees are extra.

name: Money Factor to APR
description: Converts a lease money factor to an approximate annual percentage rate.
notes: A money factor of 0.0025 is about 6 % APR.

name: Credit Utilisation Ratio
description: Divides revolving balances by credit limits; a major factor in credit scores.
notes: Keeping it below about 30 % (ideally under 10 %) helps scores.

name: Payment for a Loan with a Balloon
description: Gives the level payment when part of the loan is left as a lump sum (balloon) to be paid with the last instalment.
notes: Lower payments, but the balloon must be refinanced or paid at the end.

name: APR Including Up-Front Fees
description: Finds the annual percentage rate that makes the payments equal to the loan amount actually received after fees.
notes: This is why a loan with fees has an APR above its note rate (here about 6.19 % against 6 %).

name: Loan-to-Income Multiple
description: Gives the mortgage size as a multiple of income; many lenders cap it at about 4–5×.
notes: Regulators use it to limit household over-borrowing.

name: Effective Rate with a Compensating Balance
description: Gives the true borrowing rate when the lender requires part of the loan to stay on deposit.
notes: The borrower pays interest on money they cannot use.
